subject: Feature cost -> revenue mapping: numbers and proposals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Klein <andrew.klein@brightpulse.health>, María Gómez <maria.gomez@brightpulse.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature cost -> revenue mapping: numbers and proposals

Hi Andrew / María —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a first-pass set of numbers we discussed so you have something to work from while your team aligns on budget. I put assumptions below and attached a workbook with a per-feature, per-month tab so you can toggle volumes.

Key assumptions (call):
- Primary feature: "Patient Triage Chat" (proactive + on-demand).
- Average model call length: ~140 tokens in + 260 tokens out = ~400 tokens per session.
- Expected activations: three scenarios in workbook: 50k / 200k / 750k activations per month.
- Redwood baseline inference cost (unoptimized hosted): $500 / 1M tokens. We show target pricing bands and margin impact below.

What we propose (illustrative):
- Target commercial band A (pilot): $450 / 1M tokens — focused on speed to value and shorter pilot term.
- Band B (scaling): $350 / 1M tokens — requires 6–9 month commit and 3–6M tokens/month average.
- Band C (enterprise reserved): $250 / 1M tokens — annual reserved spend + Dedicated capacity.

Per-feature math (example, Band B):
- 400 tokens/session * 200k sessions/mo = 80M tokens/mo.
- At $350 / 1M tokens => $28k/mo inference cost.
- If you target $/feature = $5 ARR per MAU for the triage feature, 200k activations -> revenue run-rate ~1M ARR (depends on monetization).
- CAC payback target we heard from you: 6–9 months. To hit that with this unit cost, we model upsell/usage velocity in the workbook.

Next steps I recommend (short list):
1) I attached the feature-econ-workbook.xlsx — please fill in your expected activation mix for triage vs other features.
2) If procurement needs a simple pricing bands PDF for finance, I attached a draft price band sheet (redwood-pricing-bands-v1.pdf).
3) Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up with your finance/ops lead and our SRE (Karthik) — slot suggestions below.

Open questions from our end:
- Does your revenue model charge per activation or per MAU tier?
- Are there latency/SLA constraints that would push you toward Dedicated earlier?
- Do you have a hard $/1M target you need to hit to get budget approved?

I'll wait for the activation numbers and procurement timeline. Happy to re-run scenarios once you drop the volumes in the workbook.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Feature cost -> revenue mapping: numbers and proposals

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the workbook. A few clarifications from our side after I reviewed with María:

- Our preferred commercial target is between $325–$425 / 1M tokens for the pilot/POC phase — we need to show our CFO that pilot economics are under control to get to a broader trial.
- For long-term procurement, the CFO wants a 9–12 month CAC payback worst-case scenario. We can stretch to 12 months if the unit economics on the feature are strong.
- Activation mix: our initial trial will be heavy on triage (80%) with a backup "smart summaries" feature (20%). We're expecting ~120k activations/month in the first 90 days — volume could double if early metrics look good.

Can you: (A) run the workbook for a 120k / mo baseline with a $375 / 1M token mid-band, and (B) produce a short three-row pricing option we can take to procurement (pilot / scale / reserved) that includes estimated monthly inference cost and implied gross margin assuming our monetization $/feature is $3.50?

Procurement will also want a simple SLA callout and whether Dedicated is a gating requirement. We can get a finance slot for a follow-up on Thu afternoon — is Karthik available?

Thanks —
Andrew
VP Product | BrightPulse Health
andrew.klein@brightpulse.health | +1 (646) 555-0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Feature cost -> revenue mapping: numbers and proposals

Hi Andrew —

Wanted to surface a few engineering & ops considerations that materially affect the $/1M token we can offer and the margin you see: 

- Optimizations: with standard quantization + continuous batching on our hosted runtime we typically see a 20–30% reduction in per-token execution cost compared to unoptimized baseline. For your traffic profile (many short sessions), prefix/KV caching yields additional savings (~10%) for repeat conversations.
- SLA/latency: if you require <200ms p50 for interactive triage, that pushes toward reserved instances / Dedicated, which lowers unit cost but requires a commitment.
- Mixed model approach: start pilot on hosted with optimization profile "fast-batch" (lower latency, modest batching) and move to Dedicated at scale. Our pricing bands reflect this.

Attached is a quick sensitivity table I put together for the 120k activation baseline Andrew mentioned. The workbook has the full tabs, but highlights: 
- Scenario (120k activations, 400 tokens/session -> 48M tokens/mo):
  - Unoptimized baseline: $24k/mo (at $500 /1M)
  - Optimized hosted (estimated): $16.8k/mo (30% reduction)
  - Dedicated reserved rate (illustrative): $12k/mo (with annual commit)

Margin note vs $3.50 / feature monetization: at 120k activations -> revenue = $420k ARPU-year if you equate activations to paying events (model depends). The quick math shows room to hit a 40–60% gross margin at Band B (after optimizations). Exact numbers in workbook.

Happy to join the Thursday slot with finance. If Procurement wants a short technical appendix on SLA/DR, I can draft one.

-Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
